arml-local-2017-relay-1-1.title: Find a factorisation
arml-local-2017-relay-1-1.body:
$10\cdot9\cdot8=720=6!$, so $10!=6!\cdot7!$ and $(x,y)=(6,7)$ works. A larger $x$ would require $y>x\ge7$ and $x!y!\ge7!\,8!>10!$. So the maximum is $6$.

**Answer: 6**

arml-local-2017-relay-1-2.title: Square plus four triangles
arml-local-2017-relay-1-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $6$.)*

The octagon consists of the square $ARES$ (side $T$; at each of its vertices $90^\circ+60^\circ+60^\circ=210^\circ$) and four equilateral triangles $SHA$, $AIR$, $RNE$, $ETS$ of side $T$. The area is $T^2+4\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}4T^2=T^2(1+\sqrt3)=36+36\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $36+36\sqrt3$**

arml-local-2017-relay-2-1.title: Triangle inequality
arml-local-2017-relay-2-1.body:
$x<\sqrt{20}+\sqrt{17}$. Since $4<\sqrt{17},\sqrt{20}<4.5$, the sum is between $8$ and $9$ (and more precisely $\approx8.6$), so the greatest integer $x$ is $8$.

**Answer: 8**

arml-local-2017-relay-2-2.title: Even-sized subsets
arml-local-2017-relay-2-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $8$.)*

A set with $n\ge1$ elements has $2^{n-1}$ subsets of even size (half of all subsets). So $2^{n-1}=8$ and $n=4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-local-2017-relay-2-3.title: Symmetry of digit positions
arml-local-2017-relay-2-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $4$.)*

The elements of $S$ are the integers with at most three base-$T$ digits, i.e. $000_T,\dots,(T-1)(T-1)(T-1)_T$ with leading zeros allowed. In each of the three positions every digit $0,\dots,T-1$ occurs $T^2$ times, so the total digit sum is $3\cdot T^2\cdot\frac{T(T-1)}2=3\cdot16\cdot6=288$.

**Answer: 288**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-1.title: Digit sum
arml-local-2017-relay-3-1.body:
The digit sum of $9876543210$ is $45$. The eight remaining digits must sum to a multiple of $9$, so the two erased digits must sum to a multiple of $9$: $9$ (the sum is at most $17$). The pairs are $\{0,9\},\{1,8\},\{2,7\},\{3,6\},\{4,5\}$, so $5$ ways (each leaves an eight-digit number).

**Answer: 5**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-2.title: Median from an acute vertex
arml-local-2017-relay-3-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $5$.)*

Let the right angle be at $A$ and $AB=AC=2x$, so the area is $2x^2$. The median to a leg, from the other acute vertex, has length $\sqrt{(2x)^2+x^2}=x\sqrt5$, while the median to the hypotenuse is $x\sqrt2$; so the longest is $x\sqrt5=T=5$, and $x^2=5$. The area is $2x^2=10$.

**Answer: 10**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-3.title: Factor theorem
arml-local-2017-relay-3-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $10$.)*

$x=-2$ is a root: $-8+12-2p+10=0$, so $2p=14$ and $p=7$.

**Answer: 7**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-4.title: Vieta
arml-local-2017-relay-3-4.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $7$.)*

$p+q=-1$ and $pq=3$. Then $c=(p+T)(q+T)=pq+T(p+q)+T^2=3-T+T^2=3-7+49=45$.

**Answer: 45**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-5.title: Two equations
arml-local-2017-relay-3-5.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $45$.)*

Let $F$ be the number of $5$-dollar bills. Then $5F+20(45-F)=780$, so $900-15F=780$ and $F=8$.

**Answer: 8**

arml-local-2017-relay-3-6.title: Use $1001=7\cdot11\cdot13$
arml-local-2017-relay-3-6.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ is the answer to the previous problem, $8$.)*

The number is $N=10000001\,T+2342340$ and $2342340=234\cdot10\cdot1001$ is divisible by $13$. So $N\equiv10000001\,T\pmod{13}$. Since $10^6\equiv1$, $10000001=10^7+1\equiv10+1=11\pmod{13}$. Hence $N\equiv11\cdot8=88\equiv10\pmod{13}$.

**Answer: 10**
